Keacy Carty to Virat Kohli, SIX, Virat Kohli fittingly finishes things off in style! 130.8kph, short and angling down leg, the right-hander pulls hard and dispatches it over fine leg. Ninth six in the match for Kohli - the most he has hit in an ODI. He's made a mockery of this WI bowling attack. India win by 8 wickets with 50 balls to spare

Coming into the game as overwhelming favourites, it took India more than 100 deliveries to get the first breakthrough. They pulled back things well to restrict West Indies to a score <300. With the bat, it was a stroll in the park for the hosts, thanks to classy centuries from Gill and Kohli. West Indies failed to capitalise on the start provided by the openers and couldn't create any sort of pressure with the ball. A couple of dropped catches and the dew didn't help their cause either. Can they find a way to slot in Vitel Lawes and Shamar Joseph - two wicket-taking bowlers - for the next game? It's time to bring the curtains down on this encounter. Three matches and three convincing wins for India in Thiruvananthapuram. The action shifts from Coastal South West India to North East India. Tune in on Wednesday (September 30th) for the second ODI in Guwahati. Until then, goodbye and good night.
